_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Rwanda covering Kingdom of Rwanda, mwami monarchy, German/Belgian colonial manipulation of Hutu-Tutsi identities, 1959 revolution, 1994 genocide against the Tutsi, RPF victory, Kagame reconstruction, and economic transformation.

ethnic_groups.name: Hutu
ethnic_groups.notes: Majority Bantu-speaking agricultural population; pre-colonial social category hardened into ethnic identity by Belgian colonial racial classification; 1959 revolution established Hutu political dominance

ethnic_groups.name: Tutsi
ethnic_groups.notes: Historically pastoralist elite; ruled pre-colonial kingdom; Belgian-assigned 'racial' identity cards; victims of 1994 genocide (~800,000 killed); RPF led by Tutsi diaspora from Uganda; post-genocide policy discourages ethnic identification

ethnic_groups.name: Twa (Batwa)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous forest-dwelling Pygmy people; potters and entertainers in kingdom; marginalised; also targeted in genocide; oldest inhabitants

country_profile.notes_unique: Highest percentage of women in parliament globally (61%+); post-genocide policy bans ethnic identification; 'Singapore of Africa' aspiration

natural_resources.notes: Major tantalum/coltan exporter (essential for electronics); '3T' minerals (tin, tantalum, tungsten); Lake Kivu methane gas extraction (KivuWatt, 25MW); tea and coffee main agricultural exports; limited arable land due to dense population; gorilla tourism (Volcanoes NP).

military.notes: Rwanda Defence Force (RDF); among Africa's most professional militaries; deployed in Mozambique (Cabo Delgado), CAR, South Sudan; UN peacekeeping contributor; accused of supporting M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo; compulsory civic service (Ingando).

infrastructure.notes: Landlocked but excellent 4G/fiber; MTN Rwanda, Airtel; Kigali Innovation City (planned); drone delivery (Zipline).

debt_aid.notes: Aid finances ~40% of budget; Vision 2050 (transition to upper-middle income); Kigali Convention Centre; BK Arena; new Bugesera International Airport under construction; Arsenal FC and PSG sponsorship deals for tourism promotion; Volkswagen assembly plant.

top_universities: University of Rwanda (2013, merged national universities)
education.notes: Free 12-year basic education; English replaced French as medium of instruction (2009); Carnegie Mellon Africa campus; coding bootcamps (Andela Kigali); ICT in education push; high gender parity in enrollment.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 500,000+ (DR Congo, Uganda, Belgium, France, USA, Canada)
diaspora_migration.notes: 1994 genocide diaspora (Tutsi and later Hutu); hosts Congolese and Burundian refugees; diaspora investment encouraged; Rwandan refugees in neighbouring countries contentious politically.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: UK asylum deal (signed 2022, cancelled 2024 by Labour); visa-free for all Africans

digital_economy.notes: Smart Kigali initiative; 4G LTE covers 95%+ of population; Irembo e-government platform (600+ services online); drone delivery (Zipline, blood/vaccine delivery); cashless economy push; MTN Rwanda and Airtel operators.

country_profile.national_motto: Ubumwe, Umurimo, Gukunda Igihugu (Unity, Work, Patriotism)

geography.terrain: Hilly and mountainous ('land of a thousand hills'); Virunga volcanoes (northwest); Lake Kivu; grassy uplands; central plateau
geography.notes: 'Land of a Thousand Hills'; one of most densely populated in Africa; Virunga mountain gorilla habitat; 1994 genocide (800,000+ killed); dramatic transformation post-genocide.

economy_extended.notes: Fastest growing African economies; Vision 2050; Kigali master-planned; services/tech-driven growth; MICE tourism; coffee/tea exports; strong governance; UK Rwanda asylum deal (cancelled); criticized for DRC conflict involvement.

health.notes: Community-based health insurance (Mutuelle de Santé, 92% coverage); Zipline drone delivery (blood, vaccines—partnership); fastest primary healthcare improvement in Africa.

food_agriculture.notes: Land consolidation programme; crop intensification (CIP); specialty coffee export expansion; terraced hillsides; One Cow Per Poor Family (Girinka).

energy.notes: KivuWatt methane extraction from Lake Kivu (unique); Rusumo Falls hydropower (shared); rapid solar expansion; target 100% access.

transport.notes: Bugesera International Airport (under construction, $800M); RwandAir expanding routes; excellent road network for region; motorcycle taxis (motos).

tourism.notes: Gorilla permits $1500 (among most expensive wildlife experiences); MICE tourism strategy; Kigali Convention Centre; Arsenal/PSG sponsorship; Visit Rwanda brand.

human_rights_gender.notes: 61% women in parliament (highest globally); authoritarian governance; RPF dominance; limited political opposition; Kagame criticism risks; HRW/AI concerns.

active_conflicts: Alleged support for M23 in eastern DRC (UN reports)
security_stability.notes: Extremely safe domestically (Kigali safest capital in Africa); strong security apparatus; major peacekeeping contributor; DRC M23 involvement controversy.

major_festivals: Umuganda (community service day, last Sat of month)
cultural_heritage.film_industry: Growing (Rwanda Film Festival; filming location for international productions)
notable_historical_figures: Dian Fossey (primatologist, Gorillas in the Mist)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: KT Press, New Times (pro-government); state dominates; limited press freedom; social media active
cultural_heritage.notes: Post-genocide transformation; Umuganda community service; Imigongo art; gorilla conservation; 'cleanest city in Africa'; plastic bag ban pioneer (2008).

legal_system.legal_tradition: Civil law (Belgian-derived) with customary law elements
legal_system.customary_law_role: Gacaca courts (traditional justice, used for genocide trials 2005-2012)
legal_system.notes: 2015 constitutional amendment allowed Kagame third term; Gacaca courts processed ~2M genocide cases; strong contract enforcement; anti-corruption measures.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: #2 ease of doing business in Africa; highest women in parliament globally.

current_leader.name: Paul Kagame
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: RPF chairman; led RPF invasion from Uganda to stop genocide; VP 1994–2000; President 2000–; re-elected 2003, 2010, 2017, 2024 (99%+); term limits amended; praised for development; criticised for authoritarianism

former_leaders.name: Grégoire Kayibanda
former_leaders.notes: First president; Hutu; PARMEHUTU; anti-Tutsi policies; overthrown by Habyarimana

former_leaders.name: Juvénal Habyarimana
former_leaders.notes: Military dictator; MRND; his assassination (plane shot down 6 April 1994) triggered the genocide

former_leaders.name: Pasteur Bizimungu
former_leaders.notes: Hutu figurehead president under RPF; resigned; imprisoned 2002–2007

910.name: Early Settlement and Iron Age
910.description: Twa hunter-gatherer communities; Bantu migration bringing agriculture and ironworking to the Great Lakes region.

sub_clusters.name: Twa Forest Communities
sub_clusters.description: Twa (Batwa) hunter-gatherers as earliest known inhabitants of the forested highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration into Rwanda
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples settle the region; introduction of iron smelting, banana cultivation, and cattle-keeping.

920.name: Kingdom of Rwanda
920.description: Emergence of the Kingdom of Rwanda under mwami (king) rule; development of clan structures, cattle-based social organisation, and centralised monarchy.

sub_clusters.name: Origins of Mwami Monarchy
sub_clusters.description: Emergence of small Hutu and Tutsi kingdoms; gradual consolidation under Tutsi mwami dynasty.

sub_clusters.name: Expansion of the Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Rwanda kingdom expands through military conquest and cattle clientship (ubuhake); highly centralised state emerges.

sub_clusters.name: Ubuhake Clientship System
sub_clusters.description: Cattle-based patron-client relationships between Tutsi elites and Hutu agriculturalists; social stratification crystallises.

930.name: Peak of Rwandan Kingdom
930.description: Rwandan kingdom reaches maximum power under great mwami; military expansion; intore warrior traditions; first European contact.

sub_clusters.name: Reign of Kigeli IV Rwabugiri
sub_clusters.description: Rwanda's most powerful mwami; military campaigns expand borders; highly centralised administration; resists early European intrusion.

sub_clusters.name: First European Contact
sub_clusters.description: Count von Götzen becomes first European to enter Rwanda 1894; kingdom remains largely autonomous.

940.name: German and Belgian Colonial Rule
940.description: German indirect rule; Belgian League of Nations mandate; racial ideology imposed on Hutu-Tutsi identities; identity cards; growing tensions.

sub_clusters.name: German East Africa Period
sub_clusters.description: Rwanda incorporated into German East Africa; indirect rule through mwami; minimal administrative presence.

sub_clusters.name: Belgian Mandate and Trusteeship
sub_clusters.description: Belgium seizes Rwanda in WWI; League of Nations mandate; racial theories harden Hutu-Tutsi divisions.

sub_clusters.name: Ethnic Identity Cards Introduced
sub_clusters.description: Belgian administration introduces ethnic identity cards classifying all Rwandans as Hutu, Tutsi, or Twa; biological racism codified.

sub_clusters.name: Hutu Revolution of 1959
sub_clusters.description: Hutu uprising overthrows Tutsi monarchy; mwami flees; mass Tutsi refugee exodus; Belgian-supported transition.

950.name: First and Second Hutu Republics
950.description: Independence under Kayibanda; Habyarimana coup; Tutsi exile and periodic pogroms; RPF invasion from Uganda.

sub_clusters.name: Kayibanda First Republic
sub_clusters.description: Independence 1 July 1962; Grégoire Kayibanda president; Hutu dominance; anti-Tutsi violence 1963, 1967.

sub_clusters.name: Habyarimana Second Republic
sub_clusters.description: Juvénal Habyarimana seizes power; one-party MRND rule; northern Hutu elite; Tutsi excluded from power.

sub_clusters.name: RPF Invasion from Uganda
sub_clusters.description: Rwandan Patriotic Front invades from Uganda October 1990; civil war; Arusha Accords 1993.

950.name: 1994 Genocide Against the Tutsi
950.description: Systematic genocide kills approximately 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu in 100 days; RPF victory ends the genocide.

sub_clusters.name: Assassination of Habyarimana
sub_clusters.description: Presidential plane shot down 6 April 1994; genocide begins within hours; Interahamwe and army carry out mass killings.

sub_clusters.name: The Hundred Days
sub_clusters.description: Approximately 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu systematically murdered April–July 1994; international community fails to intervene.

sub_clusters.name: RPF Victory and End of Genocide
sub_clusters.description: RPF under Paul Kagame captures Kigali July 1994; genocide ends; mass Hutu refugee exodus to Zaire.

960.name: Post-Genocide Reconstruction and Modern Rwanda
960.description: Kagame-led reconstruction; Gacaca courts; economic transformation; regional military involvement; authoritarian governance debates.

sub_clusters.name: Gacaca Community Justice Courts
sub_clusters.description: Community-based transitional justice courts process nearly 2 million genocide cases; reconciliation model.

sub_clusters.name: Rwanda in Congo Wars
sub_clusters.description: Rwanda intervenes in First and Second Congo Wars; pursuit of genocide perpetrators; resource extraction controversies.

sub_clusters.name: Economic Transformation (Vision 2020/2050)
sub_clusters.description: Kagame's development model; ICT hub; Kigali modernisation; high growth rates; Singapore of Africa aspirations.

sub_clusters.name: Kagame Governance and Human Rights Debates
sub_clusters.description: Paul Kagame dominant leadership; constitutional amendments; press restrictions; international criticism alongside development success.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
